- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too high after sharp price spikes in history, then overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Model underreacts to recent downward trends in history — fails to mean-revert quickly enough.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the first 10–15 days, then stabilizes or slightly underestimates later.
- Model often ignores recent low prices in history when forecasting, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Forecasts show lag in adjusting to recent price drops — takes 2–3 days to correct downward bias.
- Model tends to overfit recent high prices, especially if the last 5–7 days are elevated.
- When history includes a sharp drop, model often fails to anticipate the drop and continues to forecast upward.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the last 10–15 days are trending downward — model adjusts better to downward momentum.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price corrections after spikes — fails to capture full mean reversion.
